declared_purpose: Provide ElevenLabs API speech synthesis with voice personas, languages, streaming, batches, sound effects, voice design and pronunciation rules; offer local setup, usage/cost monitoring, an optional budget setting and separate OpenClaw integration. Setup explicitly requires API-key input. Session retention limits and origin labels are implementation choices (SKILL.md:4, 23-41, 47-57, 327-365; scripts/setup.py:120-131, 181-197).

data_operations.operation: Collect and persist setup configuration locally
data_operations.data_scope: Required API key; selected voice, language, quality and tracking preference; optional monthly budget; configuration metadata. The key is stored as plaintext JSON.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Skill-root config.json; setup caller receives preferences and the API-key suffix in the summary.
data_operations.condition: First setup or accepted reconfiguration. Existing configuration is overwritten after collection. The wizard makes no network request. None of the supplied generators loads this configuration.

data_operations.data_scope: ELEVEN_API_KEY, falling back to ELEVENLABS_API_KEY. If neither exists, the complete skill-local .env is read to locate the first ELEVEN_API_KEY entry; other entries are not included in requests.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Generator memory and its immediate caller; subsequent authenticated API requests are listed separately.
data_operations.condition: When credential loading is reached. Missing credentials cause exit. These functions do not read config.json or OpenClaw configuration.

data_operations.operation: Read voice definitions and transform text locally
data_operations.data_scope: Voice definitions, presets and pronunciation file contents. Matching words in synthesis text are replaced case-insensitively. Voice demographic/persona labels describe configured voices rather than inferred user attributes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: TTS process memory; voice listings can return to the caller. Requests contain selected settings and transformed text, rather than the entire configuration files.
data_operations.condition: Voice definitions load before every TTS command. Pronunciations load for ordinary single/batch synthesis unless --no-pronunciations is set; --test bypasses that loading.

data_operations.operation: Read explicitly selected content files locally
data_operations.source: TTS/SFX batch handlers and documented shell example
data_operations.data_scope: Entire selected batch file; selected text/prompt, voice, output name and SFX duration fields. A documented streaming example separately reads chapter1.txt through shell substitution.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory; selected content then enters the applicable generation request.
data_operations.condition: User selects --batch or follows the shell-reading example. The batch handlers do not upload the complete JSON document as a document.

data_operations.operation: Disclose synthesis inputs for required remote TTS generation
data_operations.data_scope: Runtime API key in xi-api-key; synthesis text after applicable pronunciation replacement; selected voice ID, model, voice settings and optional language code.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ElevenLabs: https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}, with /stream appended in streaming mode.
data_operations.condition: Valid voice and credential on single, batch or --test generation. Batch generates one request per item; --test uses packaged sample sentences for every configured voice. Streaming changes response handling rather than reducing submitted text.

data_operations.operation: Disclose sound-effect inputs for required remote generation
data_operations.data_scope: Runtime API key in xi-api-key; complete prompt, prompt influence and optional duration clamped to 0.5–22 seconds.
data_operations.condition: Single generation or each selected batch item.

data_operations.operation: Disclose explicitly selected synthetic voice characteristics and preview text
data_operations.data_scope: Runtime API key; selected/default gender, age, accent and clamped accent strength; custom/default preview text. A supplied description is prepended to the text. These characteristics are design inputs, not inferred user demographics.
data_operations.condition: Voice-design invocation after validation, except --options. Generation precedes optional library saving.

data_operations.operation: Request remote persistence of a designed voice
data_operations.data_scope: Runtime API key, generated voice ID, requested name, supplied or fallback description, and labels identifying a designed voice and openclaw-skill origin.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ElevenLabs: https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voice-generation/create-voice; intended persistence in the user's ElevenLabs voice library.
data_operations.condition: --save is explicitly requested and preview generation returns a usable voice ID. The response ID and a suggested voices.json entry return to the caller; the script does not edit voices.json.

data_operations.source: TTS, SFX and voice-design response handlers
data_operations.data_scope: Returned audio bytes; voice-design responses may supply base64 audio. TTS test mode creates per-voice samples.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected/default local output files, batch destinations, or skill-root samples directory.
data_operations.condition: Audio is received. Streaming writes progressively and can leave an incomplete file on failure. Voice-design JSON responses only produce an audio file when audio_base64 is present.

data_operations.operation: Read and persist TTS usage history
data_operations.data_scope: Cumulative character/request counts, reset timestamp, and up to 1,000 sessions containing exact timestamps, transformed-text character counts and resolved voice names. Raw synthesis text is not recorded here.
data_operations.condition: Every successful audio write attempts tracking, including --test, without consulting the setup tracking preference. Existing usage files lacking expected TTS keys can prevent the update.

data_operations.operation: Read and persist SFX usage history
data_operations.data_scope: Cumulative request/second totals and up to 100 sessions containing timestamps, duration and the first 100 prompt characters. Unspecified duration is estimated as five seconds rather than measured from audio.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: The same skill-root .usage.json used by TTS.
data_operations.condition: After successful SFX audio writing, without consulting the setup tracking preference.

data_operations.operation: Derive and display local usage/cost estimates
data_operations.data_scope: Stored TTS totals, reset date and latest ten sessions; estimated costs computed from character counts and packaged plan rates. These are estimates rather than retrieved billing records.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local stdout and immediate caller; no statistics API request.
data_operations.condition: --stats; this branch returns before credential loading.

data_operations.operation: Return content-bearing progress and error output to the caller
data_operations.data_scope: Full SFX prompts, first 50 batch text/prompt characters, selected design characteristics and description prefix, saved voice metadata, and truncated provider error bodies. Error-body contents depend on the provider.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local stdout/immediate caller. Additional logging or forwarding by the host is not established.
data_operations.condition: Applicable generation, batch progress, library-save or error path.

data_operations.operation: Prune or overwrite local tracking data
data_operations.source: Session retention limits and scripts/tts.py reset_stats
data_operations.data_scope: Old TTS/SFX session entries; --reset-stats replaces the shared file with empty TTS counters/history, also dropping existing SFX fields.
data_operations.condition: History exceeds 1,000 TTS or 100 SFX entries, or --reset-stats is requested. Reset performs a local overwrite, without requesting provider deletion or deleting generated audio/configuration.

data_operations.operation: Document a separate OpenClaw configuration and execution path
data_operations.data_scope: Provider configuration with an environment credential reference or plain-string API key; conversational speech selected through automatic or one-off TTS triggers.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Documented local ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and OpenClaw's built-in TTS component. Its actual request payload and persistence are unresolved.
data_operations.condition: User follows the integration instructions. This component is explicitly separate from the packaged Python generators.

potential_excess.data_scope: All TTS/SFX usage recording when config.costTracking is false.
potential_excess.condition: Setup tracking is disabled, followed by successful TTS or SFX generation.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Setup explicitly offers a tracking choice; unconditional recording is an implementation choice and a redundant action for users who disable it.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Generate and save requested audio; preserve statistics for users who enable tracking.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Read and honor the tracking preference, skipping tracking-file reads/writes when disabled.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep generation, authentication, audio output and explicitly requested statistics reset functional.

potential_excess.data_scope: First 100 characters of each successful SFX prompt, retained across up to 100 sessions.
potential_excess.condition: Successful SFX generation, including when tracking is otherwise desired.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Usage/cost monitoring needs counts and durations; prompt excerpts add content to that persistence action without contributing to those calculations.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Submit the full requested prompt to ElevenLabs and maintain opted-in usage totals.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit stored prompt excerpts while retaining necessary request/second totals and any required duration records.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep remote generation input, generated audio and usage totals unchanged.

potential_excess.data_scope: TTS session timestamps, character counts and voice names older than the latest ten entries, up to the 1,000-entry limit.
potential_excess.condition: Tracking is enabled and more than ten TTS sessions accumulate.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The supplied statistics interface displays ten recent sessions; cumulative totals are maintained separately. Retaining the additional historical rows is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Display cumulative usage/cost estimates and the latest ten sessions.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Cap persisted TTS history at ten entries unless a larger history is explicitly requested.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve cumulative counters, reset metadata and the existing recent-session display.

potential_excess.data_scope: The labels.source value identifying openclaw-skill origin.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: ElevenLabs create-voice request at https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voice-generation/create-voice; intended voice-library metadata.
potential_excess.condition: --save with a usable generated voice ID.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Saving the requested voice is explicit. Disclosing its originating integration adds metadata to that required request; the preview/save sequence itself serves the requested outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Create the requested library voice using its generated ID, requested name and appropriate description.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit the origin label if the provider accepts its omission.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Confirm the provider schema permits omission; preserve required fields and successful library saving.

potential_excess.data_scope: Final four characters of the configured API key.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Setup summary on local stdout/immediate caller.
potential_excess.condition: Setup completes and prints its summary.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Confirming accepted credential configuration does not require returning credential characters. This is extra data in a status message, not an established remote disclosure.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Confirm that the key was accepted and configuration saved.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Display a fully masked credential status.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain validation, saved configuration and useful non-secret setup preferences.

unknowns: ElevenLabs backend retention, training use, onward disclosure and deletion are not established by the supplied source. A library-save request does not establish its internal storage policy.
Provider schemas are not supplied, so voice-design payload acceptance and whether labels.source can be omitted remain unresolved.

OpenClaw implementation is absent. Its actual speech selection, requests, credential handling and retention cannot be verified. The older example configuration also differs from the corrected entry instructions (examples.md:425-438; SKILL.md:334-358; CHANGELOG.md:5-8).

The advertised setup-to-runtime connection is unresolved: the generators never load config.json, so saved credentials/preferences do not configure them and no supplied consumer enforces the monthly budget warning (scripts/setup.py:181-208; scripts/tts.py:207-226, 502-559; scripts/sfx.py:32-46, 297-320; scripts/voice-design.py:48-61, 289-324).

The claimed .gitignore exclusion cannot be verified: no .gitignore is present in the supplied inventory. Actual file permissions, backups and host capture of stdout are also unknown (README.md:12; SKILL.md:41).

The wizard's locally stored key is not the credential source used by the generators. The entry's 'never leaves your machine' assurance must therefore be distinguished from runtime environment/.env credentials, which are sent in authentication headers (SKILL.md:41; scripts/tts.py:207-219, 296-318; scripts/sfx.py:107-124; scripts/voice-design.py:95-113).
